thesis: Frontier AI is a small number of very large pretrained Transformers, built on NVIDIA clusters from web-scale human text and sold as closed metered APIs behind a chat box. Capability is bought with pretraining scale. The models are expensive to run, frozen after release, retain nothing between conversations, and answer requests rather than carry out work.

dimensions.name: Compute
dimensions.baseline: Frontier capability requires massive centralised compute.
dimensions.incentive: Reduce the compute and cost required for frontier capability.
dimensions.inflection: Frontier-level capability becomes achievable under fundamentally different compute economics.
evidence: GPT-4 training compute widely estimated in the tens of thousands of A100-years — 2023-03
Llama 2 trained on a 2,000-GPU A100 cluster — 2023-07
Inflection announces a 22,000-H100 cluster — 2023-06
H100 lead times reported at 6-11 months; sustained shortage through the year — 2023-08
CoWoS advanced packaging named as the binding supply constraint — 2023
Frontier training runs priced in the tens of millions of dollars — 2023

dimensions.name: Architecture
dimensions.baseline: Transformers are the dominant frontier architecture.
dimensions.incentive: Improve capability or efficiency beyond what the dominant architecture permits.
dimensions.inflection: A different architecture or capability mechanism meaningfully challenges Transformer dominance at the frontier.
evidence: Attention Is All You Need — 2017-06
Every frontier model released this year is a Transformer: GPT-4, Claude 2, Gemini 1, Llama 2 — 2023
FlashAttention-2 optimises the Transformer rather than replacing it — 2023-07
Mamba proposes a selective state-space alternative, at small scale and unproven at the frontier — 2023-12
RWKV and RetNet published as recurrent alternatives, neither at frontier scale — 2023

dimensions.name: Scaling
dimensions.baseline: Capability is primarily produced by larger pretraining runs on more human text.
dimensions.incentive: Find additional ways to increase capability beyond pretraining scale.
dimensions.inflection: A new scaling axis materially changes how additional capability is produced.
evidence: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models — 2020-01
Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models (Chinchilla) — 2022-03
GPT-4 Technical Report attributes capability to scale and predictable scaling — 2023-03
Chain-of-Thought prompting raises measured capability without retraining, and is read as a prompting technique rather than a scaling axis — 2022-01
Projections that high-quality public text is exhausted within the decade — 2022-10

dimensions.name: Access
dimensions.baseline: Frontier capability is concentrated in a small number of closed providers.
dimensions.incentive: Make frontier capability cheaper, open or broadly accessible.
dimensions.inflection: Frontier capability becomes available through a materially different ownership or distribution model.
evidence: GPT-4, Claude 2 and Gemini 1 released as closed metered APIs — 2023
Llama 2 released under a community licence with use restrictions — 2023-07
Mistral 7B and Mixtral 8x7B released under Apache 2.0, below frontier capability — 2023-09, 2023-12
Best open-weight models trail the closed frontier on public leaderboards throughout the year — 2023
Adapting a frontier model to private work is limited to prompting and restricted fine-tuning endpoints — 2023

dimensions.name: Agency
dimensions.baseline: Models respond to requests; they do not carry out extended work.
dimensions.incentive: Make models able to reliably complete useful work with less human intervention.
dimensions.inflection: Models move from responding to requests to reliably executing extended work.
evidence: ChatGPT and Claude.ai are turn-taking chat interfaces — 2022-11, 2023-07
ReAct interleaves reasoning and tool calls within a single task — 2022-10
Toolformer teaches self-supervised API calls — 2023-02
AutoGPT, BabyAGI and Voyager attempt autonomous multi-step execution and are widely reported as unreliable beyond short horizons — 2023-04, 2023-05
Models are confidently wrong in ways they cannot detect, compounding over multi-step tasks — 2023

dimensions.name: Persistence
dimensions.baseline: Models are static after training and retain nothing across interactions.
dimensions.incentive: Let a deployed model accumulate and retain what it encounters, cheaply.
dimensions.inflection: A deployed model's capability improves from its own use without a new training run.
evidence: Weights are frozen at release; capability changes only through a new training run — 2023
Retrieval-Augmented Generation supplies context at inference and leaves weights untouched — 2020-05
LangChain and LlamaIndex ship external memory as application plumbing — 2023
MemGPT proposes paged virtual context to simulate longer memory — 2023-10
LoRA makes adaptation cheap but is an offline training step, not learning from use — 2021-06
